shots.desc: Jerusalem, a bright morning. Saul, a young man with a dark beard and a frown, stomps up to the high priest's porch, fists tight. The old high priest, calm and unsmiling, hands him a rolled-up letter. Saul holds it up and marches off.
The hot desert road: sand, rocks, one palm. Saul marches ahead with the letter in his belt; two temple guards, one tall and thin, one short and round, puff along behind him. He stops and scolds them.

Near the city, at noon. Suddenly a great light, brighter than the sun, pours down from the sky all round Saul: warm white and gold, wonderful, not frightening. Saul shields his eyes and sits down hard in the road; the two guards duck and cover their heads.

Saul sits in the road inside the light, one arm up against the brightness, looking up. A voice speaks from the light: it is Jesus. Behind him the guards peep out from under their arms: they hear a sound but see no one.
The light is gone. Saul stands up with his eyes open but sees nothing; he holds his hands out. The tall guard takes his hand and leads him slowly to the city gate; the short guard walks behind.
Inside Judas's house on Straight Street. Saul sits on a mat with his eyes closed, praying, a soft glow round him. Kind Judas offers him bread; Saul gently shakes his head and goes on praying.

Ananias's little house down the street. Ananias, a small round man with a grey beard, kneels to pray. A soft light fills the room and the Lord speaks to him. When he hears the name Saul he jumps up, knees knocking; then he swallows hard and goes.

Ananias tiptoes along Straight Street to Judas's door and knocks. Inside, he puts his hands gently on Saul's head. Something like little scales falls from Saul's eyes, sparkling; Saul blinks and sees. His face lights up.
Saul kneels and Ananias pours water over his head from a jug: he is baptised, and he laughs. Then Judas brings bread, and Saul eats hungrily and happily.
The synagogue steps on Straight Street. Saul stands on the top step, arms open, telling everyone about Jesus. The two temple guards stand at the side, scratching their heads: is this the same Saul?

Night outside the city wall, torches by the gate. The short guard boasts, then dozes on his feet; the tall guard holds up a lantern and peers down the road. Behind their backs a big basket comes down the wall on two ropes from a high window. Saul climbs out, waves up to the window and tiptoes away.
Back in Jerusalem, at the door of the believers' house. Peter peeks out and shrinks back, afraid of Saul. Big, kind Barnabas comes up and speaks up for Saul. Peter smiles and hugs him.

The whole page in warm sunshine: Damascus, the road, Jerusalem. Everyone stands in a row along the front and waves to the child: Ananias, Judas, Saul, Barnabas, Peter, and even the two guards, who have stopped frowning.

lines.zh: 耶路撒冷有个年轻人叫扫罗。他很生气，想把跟随耶稣的人都抓起来。
lines.en: In Jerusalem lived a young man called Saul. He was angry, and wanted to arrest everyone who followed Jesus.
lines.dir: storyteller, clear and lively; plain and calm on 抓 / 'arrest' (the only sentence about it), a small frown on 生气 / 'angry'

lines.zh: 大祭司，给我写几封信吧！我要去大马士革，把他们都带回来！
lines.en: High priest, give me letters! I'll go to Damascus and bring them all back!
lines.dir: young, hot-headed, sure of himself; loud but not shouting; a stamp on 都 / 'all'

lines.zh: 好吧，信在这里。去吧。
lines.en: Very well. Here are your letters. Go.
lines.dir: an old, dry, calm voice; neither kind nor cruel; unhurried

lines.zh: 扫罗带着两个卫兵出发了。路又长又热。
lines.en: Saul set off with two guards. The road was long and hot.
lines.dir: brisk, a marching rhythm in the words

lines.zh: 扫罗大人，歇一会儿吧！我的脚都走扁了！
lines.en: Master Saul, can we rest? My feet are flat as pancakes!
lines.dir: a round, puffing comic voice; out of breath; whiny, funny

lines.zh: 不歇！大马士革就在前面。走！
lines.en: No rest! Damascus is just ahead. March!
lines.dir: impatient, bossy, clipped

lines.zh: 忽然，一道比太阳还亮的光从天上照下来！扫罗一下子坐倒在地上。
lines.en: Suddenly a light brighter than the sun shone from heaven, and Saul fell to the ground.
lines.dir: wonder, building fast; bright and amazed, never scary; a soft drop on the fall

lines.zh: 扫罗，扫罗，你为什么跟我作对？
lines.en: Saul, Saul, why are you against Me?
lines.dir: calm, warm, very clear; sad and loving, not angry; the same Jesus as in Real Miracles

lines.zh: 主啊，你是谁？
lines.en: Lord... who are You?
lines.dir: small and shaken, all the anger gone; almost a whisper

lines.zh: 我就是耶稣。你跟我的朋友作对，就是跟我作对。
lines.en: I am Jesus. When you are against My friends, you are against Me.
lines.dir: gentle and firm; the heart of the scene; slow on 我就是耶稣 / 'I am Jesus'

lines.zh: 起来，进城去，会有人告诉你该做什么。
lines.en: Get up and go into the city. You will be told what to do.
lines.dir: kind, a fresh start in the voice

lines.zh: 有声音……可是一个人也没有！
lines.en: I heard a voice... but there's nobody here!
lines.dir: whispered, wide-eyed, comic

lines.zh: 我睁着眼睛，可是……什么也看不见。
lines.en: My eyes are open... but I can't see anything.
lines.dir: quiet, puzzled, not afraid; slow

lines.zh: 卫兵拉着扫罗的手，慢慢把他领进了大马士革。
lines.en: So the guards took Saul by the hand and led him into Damascus.
lines.dir: tender, slow, walking pace

lines.zh: 在犹大家里，扫罗三天看不见，不吃也不喝，一直祷告。
lines.en: At Judas's house, Saul could not see for three days. He did not eat; he prayed.
lines.dir: gentle, unhurried; no sadness on 不吃也不喝 / 'did not eat'

lines.zh: 主耶稣，我错了。你要我做什么？
lines.en: Lord Jesus, I was wrong. What do You want me to do?
lines.dir: a quiet, honest prayer; humble, eyes closed; no tears

lines.zh: 亚拿尼亚，去直街犹大的家，找一个叫扫罗的人。他正在祷告。
lines.en: Ananias, go to Judas's house on Straight Street. Saul is there, praying.
lines.dir: calm, kind, calling a friend

lines.zh: 扫罗？是那个扫罗？！主啊，他是来抓你的人的呀！
lines.en: Saul? THAT Saul?! But Lord, he came to arrest Your people!
lines.dir: the comic beat: an older, fussy voice squeaking in alarm, words tumbling out; frightened in a funny way

lines.zh: 去吧！我拣选了他，要他把我告诉全世界。
lines.en: Go! I have chosen him to tell the whole world about Me.
lines.dir: patient, warm, a smile in it; no scolding

lines.zh: 好……好吧，主，我去。
lines.en: All... all right, Lord. I'll go.
lines.dir: a big gulp, then brave; a little laugh at himself at the end

lines.zh: 亚拿尼亚有点害怕，可他还是去了。
lines.en: Ananias was a bit scared, but he went.
lines.dir: playful storyteller, a twinkle

lines.zh: 扫罗弟兄，主耶稣差我来，叫你能再看见，被圣灵充满。
lines.en: Brother Saul, Jesus sent me, so you can see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit.
lines.dir: gentle and brave; a warm weight on 弟兄 / 'Brother'

lines.zh: 立刻，好像有鳞片从扫罗的眼睛上掉了下来！
lines.en: At once, something like scales fell from Saul's eyes!
lines.dir: a delighted lift, wonder

lines.zh: 我看见了！你……你叫我弟兄？
lines.en: I can see! You... you called me brother?
lines.dir: joy bursting out; then quiet, moved, amazed at 弟兄 / 'brother'

lines.zh: 是啊，现在你是我们的弟兄了！
lines.en: Yes! Now you are our brother!
lines.dir: warm, glad, a happy chuckle inside the words

lines.zh: 扫罗受了洗，又吃了饭，力气也回来了。
lines.en: Saul was baptised. Then he ate, and his strength came back.
lines.dir: bright and happy

lines.zh: 这饼真香！三天没吃了！
lines.en: This bread is so good! Three days with nothing!
lines.dir: mouth half full, laughing, a big grin; the old anger quite gone

lines.zh: 耶稣是神的儿子！他救了我，他也爱你们！
lines.en: Jesus is the Son of God! He saved me, and He loves you too!
lines.dir: glad, warm, strong; the same voice as the angry Saul, now full of joy

lines.zh: 咦，这不是那个来抓人的扫罗吗？
lines.en: Hey, isn't that the Saul who came to arrest people?
lines.dir: thin, puzzled, comic

lines.zh: 他……他完全变了！
lines.en: He's... he's completely changed!
lines.dir: gruff, baffled, comic

lines.zh: 有些人很生气，日夜守着城门，要抓扫罗。
lines.en: Now some angry men watched the gate day and night, to catch Saul.
lines.dir: a little hush, mock-suspense; not scary

lines.zh: 有我们守着，连一只老鼠也跑不掉！
lines.en: Nobody gets past us. Not even a mouse!
lines.dir: puffed-up, boastful, comic; a yawn creeping into the end

lines.zh: 可是夜里，朋友们让扫罗坐进大筐子，从城墙的窗户里放了下去！
lines.en: But at night, his friends let Saul down from a window in the wall, in a big basket!
lines.dir: tiptoe storytelling, quiet and twinkly

lines.zh: 慢一点……慢一点……好，到地了！
lines.en: Slowly... slowly... there, he's down!
lines.dir: from up in the window, a loud whisper, fussy and kind

lines.zh: 谢谢你们，弟兄们！
lines.en: Thank you, brothers!
lines.dir: a happy whisper up to the window

lines.zh: 扫罗回到耶路撒冷，可是大家都很怕他。
lines.en: Back in Jerusalem, Jesus's friends were afraid of Saul.
lines.dir: gentle, a small worry in it

lines.zh: 扫罗？他……他是来抓我们的吧？
lines.en: Saul? Has he... has he come to arrest us?
lines.dir: big Peter, small voice; worried, comic

lines.zh: 彼得，别怕！他遇见了耶稣，耶稣改变了他的心。
lines.en: Don't be afraid, Peter! He met Jesus, and Jesus changed his heart.
lines.dir: big, warm, encouraging; a friend's arm in the voice

lines.zh: 那……欢迎你，扫罗弟兄！
lines.en: Then... welcome, brother Saul!
lines.dir: a slow smile, then a big glad welcome

lines.zh: 耶稣把扫罗的心从生气变成了爱。后来，他叫保罗。
lines.en: Jesus turned Saul's heart from anger to love. Later, he was called Paul.
lines.dir: joyful and sure; a happy surprise on 保罗 / 'Paul'

lines.zh: 耶稣原谅了我。他能改变任何人的心！
lines.en: Jesus forgave me. He can change anyone's heart!
lines.dir: straight to the child, warm, amazed and glad

lines.zh: 上帝能改变每一个人的心。被原谅的心，也会原谅别人。
lines.en: God can change anyone's heart. And a forgiven heart learns to forgive.
lines.dir: warm, slow, a hush on the last words
